summary: Pend Oreille County summit with a 1925 platform tower and a 72-foot L-6 tower built 1937; toppled by vandals in 1975. WillhiteWeb photo captions show footings marked 2026 and cab remnants nearby.

facts.design: 72' treated timber L-6 tower with frame cabin (1937), after a 1925 log cabin and platform tower and a 1929 cupola cabin
facts.status_note: Tower toppled by vandals in 1975 and never replaced; WillhiteWeb photo captions show footings marked 2026 at the south summit and cab remnants about 80 feet from them

staffing.status: Ernest Hart in 1930; Earle Gray in 1957 and 1958; not manned in 1960; no later staffing found in the sources read

access.note: Most roads nearby are gated; the route ends at an old gate with a tank trap, and a wildlife closure area permanently ended the road. No current permit or closure notice found in the sources read.

visit.trail_note: No tower stands. WillhiteWeb's route: about 1 mile up Middle Fork Road, roughly 8 miles on Power Lake Road, then a trail for the last part. WillhiteWeb lists the hike at 2.2 miles one-way.

events.note: Log cabin and platform observation tower developed on the south end of the summit (register)
Cupola cabin built on the north end (register); Division of Forestry report says Boyer Mountain went into operation in 1929
June 19, 1930 Newport Miner item: Ernest Hart to be stationed at Boyer; WillhiteWeb names him as the 1930 lookout
72-foot treated timber L-6 tower with frame cabin living quarters built on the south summit
Newport Miner, July 2, 1942: eight Newport district lookouts being manned that week, the first being Boyer Mountain
State officials called in one Boyer lookout while continuing five others (Statesman Examiner item, September 14, 1951, quoted by Forest Lookouts)
Earle Gray was the lookout in 1957 and 1958
Would not be manned that year; money redirected to plane patrol after lightning storms (Spokane Daily Chronicle)
Toppled by vandals in 1975 and never replaced
Registered November 23, 2012; nominated by Ray Kresek

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register and Firelookout.com give 5,252 feet; WillhiteWeb gives 5,280 feet. The story uses the register figure and reports both.

The register dates the first log cabin and platform tower to 1925, while the Division of Forestry report quoted by Forest Lookouts says Boyer Mountain went into operation in 1929. The story gives both dates and does not choose.

sources.title: Boyer Mountain on Blue Grouse Mountain

notes_for_editor: Brief lists access as unknown; set to restricted from WillhiteWeb's description of gates and a wildlife closure, and no current closure notice was found, so the editor should confirm before publishing the access line. Status and 2026 remains come only from WillhiteWeb photo captions, not from text. Register photos are credited to others with no license, so none were added. The brief's registration number is US 1485 (WA 385 per the register).
